questions.q: Visual programming is best described as a style of programming that:
o: lets users illustrate processes graphically rather than writing text-based code that forces machine-like thinking
runs only inside a web browser
compiles C code into assembly automatically
questions.e: Visual programming lets developers describe a process using human-understandable graphical elements, as opposed to traditional text-based coding where the developer must think like a machine.

questions.q: Which visual programming language lets users build stories, games and animations by assembling blocks instead of writing lines of code?
questions.e: Scratch lets users create stories, games and animations purely by building the logic and assembling blocks, with no code written.

questions.q: The Blockly visual language is used to create block-based editors and generate code to target languages such as:
o: JavaScript, Lua, Dart, Python and PHP
questions.e: Blockly builds block-based programming languages/editors and can generate code from blocks into JavaScript, Lua, Dart, Python, PHP, and similar languages.

questions.q: The mBlock visual programming language is primarily used for:
questions.e: mBlock is a block-based language aimed at programming robots.

questions.q: Which visual programming language is used to create web applications?
questions.e: Bubble is a visual language used specifically for building web applications.

questions.q: Minibloq is described as a graphical programming environment for:
questions.e: Minibloq is a graphical programming environment used with Arduino hardware.

questions.q: A graphical user interface (GUI) is a digital interface in which a user interacts with:
o: graphical components such as icons, buttons and menus
questions.e: A GUI lets users interact through graphical components — icons, buttons, menus — whose visuals convey information and available actions.

questions.q: The main purpose of a Rapid Application Development (RAD) tool is to:
o: compile code to machine language faster
remove the need for any user interface
increase the size of source code
build applications quickly without coding everything from scratch
questions.e: RAD tools enable developers to build applications quickly (via rapid prototyping and development) without coding from scratch, meeting user requirements easily.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of RAD tools?
o: a drag-and-drop editor with reusable templates
exclusive access for expert programmers only
no monitoring of the development lifecycle
questions.e: RAD tool features include reusable templates, a drag-and-drop editor, monitoring the whole development lifecycle, and letting users with limited technical knowledge build apps.

questions.q: Which of the following is a RAD tool?
questions.e: Top RAD tools include Quixy, Zoho Creator, OutSystems, Appian, Nintex, Oracle Application Express and Microsoft PowerApps.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of visual programming?
o: it always outperforms hand-written machine code
it removes the need for debugging
it requires no software at all
it is easier to learn because it uses graphical symbols, making it more accessible to beginners
questions.e: Advantages include being easier to learn (graphical symbols/visual elements), simpler debugging, efficiency and speed, better retention of instructions, and the ability to create complex visual output.

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of visual programming?
o: it cannot create graphs or visualizations
it can only produce text output
directly accessing and modifying the underlying code is harder due to the graphical interface
questions.e: Disadvantages include difficulty directly manipulating the underlying code, less flexibility/robustness than traditional languages, debugging challenges when visuals obscure logic, and often needing specialized software.

questions.q: Compared with a traditional text-based language, a visual programming language mainly differs in that it:
o: forces the developer to think like a machine
lets the developer explain the process in human-understandable terms
questions.e: A visual language enables developers to explain a process in words understandable to humans, whereas text-based coding forces the developer to think like a machine.

questions.q: .NET itself is best described as:
o: a developer platform of tools, languages and libraries for building many types of applications
questions.e: .NET is a developer platform made up of tools, programming languages and libraries for building many different kinds of applications, with implementations that run on many operating systems.

questions.q: The original .NET Framework implementation supports running applications on:
questions.e: The .NET Framework is the original implementation and supports websites, services and desktop apps only on Windows.

questions.q: A key distinguishing feature of .NET Core (compared with the classic .NET Framework) is that it is:
o: cross-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS) and open source on GitHub
questions.e: .NET Core is a cross-platform implementation running on Windows, Linux and macOS, and it is open source on GitHub.

questions.q: Xamarin/Mono is the .NET implementation used for running apps on:
o: the major mobile operating systems including iOS and Android
questions.e: Xamarin/Mono is the .NET implementation for running applications on the major mobile operating systems, including iOS and Android.

questions.q: The Common Language Runtime (CLR) is best described as:
o: the run-time environment that executes .NET applications
questions.e: The CLR is the run-time environment that executes .NET apps, handling code execution, exception handling, resource management, garbage collection, code access security, JIT compilation, and more.

questions.q: In the .NET context, 'JIT' stands for:
questions.e: JIT stands for Just-In-Time compilation; the CLR's JIT compiler translates CIL into binary/native code during program execution.

questions.q: The intermediate language into which .NET source code is compiled was originally called MSIL and is now known as:
questions.e: Source code compiles to Common Intermediate Language (CIL); it was originally named Microsoft Intermediate Language (MSIL).

questions.q: When C# source code is compiled in .NET, the C# compiler produces:
questions.e: The C# compiler converts source code into CIL; the JIT compiler later turns that CIL into binary code at execution time.

questions.q: During execution, the CLR's JIT compiler translates CIL code into:
questions.e: The JIT compiler performs real-time translation of CIL into binary (native) code as the program runs.

questions.q: In the .NET runtime, the garbage collector serves as:
o: an automatic memory manager that allocates and releases memory
questions.e: The garbage collector is the CLR's automatic memory manager, allocating and releasing memory without manual intervention.

questions.q: The Framework Class Library (FCL) organizes its classes, interfaces, structures and delegates using:
questions.e: The FCL is a library of reusable, tested code consisting of classes, interfaces, structures and delegates, categorized using namespaces.

questions.q: The Common Type System (CTS) ensures that, for example, an integer variable of VB.NET transferred to an integer variable of C#:
questions.e: CTS guarantees that objects written in different .NET-compliant languages can communicate without losing data when a type in one language transfers data to a similar type in another.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the CLR's stated responsibilities?
questions.e: The CLR handles automatic memory management, code access security, garbage collection and JIT compilation; designing a database schema is not a CLR responsibility.

questions.q: Because .NET languages such as VB.NET, C# and F# all compile to CIL, .NET provides:
questions.e: Language independence: multiple CLS-compatible languages (VB.NET, C#, F#, etc.) compile to CIL, which the JIT then turns into native code, enabling interoperability.

questions.q: The two commonly cited core components of the .NET Framework are:
questions.e: The core components include the CLR (Common Language Runtime, the execution engine) and the FCL (Framework Class Library, the reusable code library).

questions.q: The .NET framework resolves 'DLL Hell' by:
o: merging all DLLs into one file
enabling the coexistence of multiple versions of the same DLL
questions.e: DLL Hell (conflicts when applications share a common DLL) is eliminated in .NET by allowing multiple versions of the same DLL to coexist.

questions.q: In terms of memory management, C++ uses:
o: manual management (pointers and explicit resource control)
questions.e: C++ uses manual memory management with pointers, requiring explicit management of resources — unlike C# and Java, which use automatic garbage collection.

questions.q: C# source code is compiled to:
o: Intermediate Language (IL) that runs on the .NET runtime
questions.e: C# compiles to Intermediate Language (IL), which then runs on the .NET runtime; memory is managed automatically via garbage collection.

questions.q: Java source code is compiled to bytecode, which runs on:
questions.e: Java compiles to bytecode that executes on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), giving its 'write once, run anywhere' capability.

questions.q: Java's 'WORA' capability stands for:
questions.e: WORA — 'write once, run anywhere' — is a key Java feature enabled by its bytecode running on the JVM across platforms.

questions.q: HTML is classified as:
o: a markup language used to define the structure and layout of web pages
questions.e: HTML is a markup language (not a programming language); it defines the structure and layout of web pages and is not compiled.

questions.q: HTML is processed by being:
questions.e: HTML is not compiled; it is interpreted directly by web browsers, and integrates with CSS and JavaScript for styling and behavior.

questions.q: The Common Type System's guarantee is illustrated by transferring data between:
o: a VB.NET integer variable and a C# integer variable without data loss
questions.e: CTS ensures data is not lost when, for example, a VB.NET integer variable transfers its value to a C# integer variable.

questions.q: The machine-independent intermediate code that provides .NET portability was originally called MSIL and later renamed:
questions.e: Portability comes from compiling to intermediate, machine-independent code originally called Microsoft Intermediate Language (MSIL), later renamed Common Intermediate Language (CIL).

questions.q: C++ code is compiled:
o: to IL that runs on the .NET runtime
questions.e: C++ is compiled directly to machine code, making it close to the hardware and high-performance, at the cost of manual memory management.

questions.q: C# manages memory through:
questions.e: C# uses automatic garbage collection for memory management, integrated with the .NET framework.

questions.q: The Base Class Library (BCL) in .NET is available to:
questions.e: The BCL is a library available to all .NET languages, offering classes for common functionality like database interaction, file I/O, image design and XML/JSON manipulation.

questions.q: In the .NET context, 'IDE' stands for:
questions.e: IDE stands for Integrated Development Environment — the software tool providing features, controls, designers and forms needed to build .NET applications.

questions.q: Automatic and efficient resource management in .NET (of memory, screen space, network connections) is made possible by:
questions.e: Automatic resource management in .NET is enabled by the CLR, whose garbage collector acts as an automatic memory manager.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical use case for C#?
o: Windows applications, web services via ASP.NET, and game development with Unity
questions.e: C# use cases include Windows applications, web services (via ASP.NET), game development (with Unity) and enterprise applications.

questions.q: A console application follows which computing model?
o: the IPO (input-process-output) model, executing statements sequentially
questions.e: Console applications run the IPO model: each line in Main() executes sequentially and control returns to Main, then the program halts.

questions.q: A Windows Forms application, once launched, primarily follows which model?
o: event-driven model, sitting in a process loop waiting for events
questions.e: Windows applications run an event-driven model: after launching, the app sits in a process loop and waits for events to execute.

questions.q: In Windows programming, an 'event' is:
o: a notification from the OS that an action such as a mouse click or key press has occurred
questions.e: An event is a notification from the operating system that an action (e.g. the user clicking the mouse or pressing a key) has occurred.

questions.q: To specify what should happen when an event occurs, a programmer must write methods called:
questions.e: Event handlers are the methods written to indicate what should be done when a particular event occurs.

questions.q: In the heading 'public class Form1 : Form', the colon indicates that Form1:
o: is derived (inherits) from the base class Form
questions.e: The colon is a separator meaning Form1 (the derived class) inherits from the base class Form, so Form1 gains the Form class's members.

questions.q: Setting a form's Text property changes its:
questions.e: The Text property is used for getting/setting the title bar caption of a form.

questions.q: Calling Application.Run(winForm) in Main() serves to:
o: place the application in its process loop
questions.e: The call to the Run() method places the application in the process loop, where it waits for events.

questions.q: In a Visual Studio Windows Forms application, the Main() method (where execution begins) is located in which file?
questions.e: Execution begins in Main(), which is located in the Program.cs file of the application.

questions.q: Every standard Windows Forms control ultimately derives from which class?
questions.e: Controls such as Button, Label, TextBox and ListBox are all classes derived from System.Windows.Forms.Control.

questions.q: To build a Windows Forms application, a program references and imports which namespace?
questions.e: Windows applications reference and import the System.Windows.Forms namespace to use forms and controls.

questions.q: Setting a TextBox's PasswordChar property to a character causes the box to:
questions.e: If PasswordChar is set to a char, the TextBox becomes a password box that masks the entered characters.

questions.q: Which TextBox property, when set to true, turns a single-line text box into a multi-line editor?
questions.e: The Multiline property (a Boolean) determines whether the TextBox is a single-line or multi-line text editor.

questions.q: Radio buttons differ from checkboxes in that radio buttons in the same container:
o: can all be checked at once
allow only one to be checked at a time
questions.e: Radio buttons grouped in the same container (usually a group box or panel) allow only one to be checked at a time, unlike independent checkboxes.

questions.q: Which event is raised when a CheckBox is checked or unchecked?
questions.e: The CheckedChanged delegate/event is invoked when the box is checked or unchecked; the Checked property gives its Boolean state.

questions.q: When arbitrary objects are added to a ListBox, the text shown for each item is produced by:
questions.e: Any object can be placed in a ListBox; its displayed text is generated by the object's ToString() method.

questions.q: For a ComboBox, the DropDownStyle value 'DropDownList' means the text is:
o: editable and the list is always visible
not editable, and the user must click to see the list
questions.e: DropDownList makes the value non-editable and requires the user to click to reveal the list (unlike Simple or DropDown, which allow editing).

questions.q: Which PictureBox property determines what happens when the image does not fit the window (e.g. StretchImage, Zoom, CenterImage)?
questions.e: The PictureBox SizeMode property (Normal, StretchImage, AutoSize, CenterImage, Zoom) determines how an image is handled when it does not fit the box.

questions.q: The NumericUpDown control, which allows selecting an integer from a limited range, is also called a:
questions.e: The NumericUpDown control is also called a spinner, with Minimum, Maximum, Increment and Value properties.

questions.q: A key difference between DateTimePicker and MonthCalendar is that DateTimePicker:
o: selects a single value rather than a range
questions.e: MonthCalendar selects a range of dates, whereas the DateTimePicker selects a single value (and is more configurable).

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut starts a Windows application with debugging in Visual Studio?
questions.e: F5 is Start Debugging; Ctrl+F5 is Start Without Debugging. (F7 shows the Code Editor and Shift+F7 the Designer.)

questions.q: The Form1 class in a simple Windows application is split across which two files as partial class definitions?
questions.e: Form1.cs (normally the only one you edit) and Form1.Designer.cs (auto-generated code) both contain partial class definitions of the Form1 class.

questions.q: A button's automatically generated click event-handler method has which signature?
o: private void btnCompute_Click(object sender, System.EventArgs e)
questions.e: Double-clicking a button generates a handler like private void btnCompute_Click(object sender, System.EventArgs e), and registers the Click event.

questions.q: A Label control is primarily used to:
o: provide descriptive text or labels for other controls
questions.e: Label objects provide descriptive text or labels for other controls; they display static text or an image rather than accepting input.

questions.q: How many types of dialog boxes are identified?
questions.e: There are three types of dialog boxes: modeless, modal, and system modal.

questions.q: A modal dialog box:
o: blocks every application on the system
allows interaction with the application while open
blocks interaction with the application until it is dismissed
questions.e: A modal dialog box blocks interaction with the application until it is dismissed.

questions.q: A modeless dialog box:
o: allows interaction with the application while it is open
must be dismissed before doing anything
questions.e: A modeless dialog box allows interaction with the application while open; control can be transferred away from it to another window (common in the Windows control panel).

questions.q: A system modal dialog box:
o: blocks interaction with only the current window
blocks interaction with all applications until it is dismissed
is the same as a modeless box
questions.e: A system modal dialog box blocks interaction with all applications until it is dismissed.

questions.q: The abstract FileDialog class is used through which concrete classes?
questions.e: The file dialog is an abstract class used via OpenFileDialog and SaveFileDialog; reusing one instance lets it remember the last directory.

questions.q: The Filter property of a file dialog is used to:
o: indicate which types of files are displayed
questions.e: Filter is a string indicating the types of files to display, given as pairs of display name and pattern separated by vertical bars, e.g. 'JPEG|*.jpg|GIF|*.gif'.

questions.q: After calling ShowDialog(), a program typically checks whether the returned value equals:
questions.e: ShowDialog() shows the dialog and blocks until OK or Cancel; code checks 'if (dialog.ShowDialog() == DialogResult.OK)' before using the selection.

questions.q: Modeless dialog boxes are commonly used in the:
questions.e: Modeless dialog boxes are frequently used as a quick way to create a window and are common in the Windows control panel.

questions.q: In the image-upload handler, after 'if (ofd.ShowDialog() == DialogResult.OK)', the selected image is loaded into a PictureBox by:
questions.e: The code sets pictureBox1.Image = new Bitmap(ofd.FileName) (and puts the path in a text box) once the user confirms the OpenFileDialog with OK.

questions.q: An exception in C# is:
o: a problem/response that arises during program execution, such as dividing by zero
a syntax error caught at compile time
questions.e: An exception is a problem that arises during the execution of a program — a response to an exceptional situation at run time, such as an attempt to divide by zero.

questions.q: C# exception handling is built upon which four keywords?
questions.e: C# exception handling uses four keywords: try (marks a guarded block), catch (handles an exception), finally (always executes), and throw (raises an exception).

questions.q: The finally block is used to execute a set of statements:
o: only when an exception is thrown
only when no exception is thrown
whether or not an exception is thrown
questions.e: The finally block runs whether or not an exception is thrown — e.g. closing a file must happen regardless of whether an exception occurred.

questions.q: The try block in C# exception handling is used to:
o: identify a block of code for which particular exceptions will be activated
questions.e: A try block identifies a block of code for which specific exceptions will be activated; it is followed by one or more catch blocks.

questions.q: The throw keyword is used to:
o: raise (throw) an exception when a problem occurs
questions.e: A program throws an exception when a problem shows up, using the throw keyword — e.g. throw new NegativeNumberException(...).

questions.q: Exception classes in C# are mainly derived (directly or indirectly) from which base class?
questions.e: C# exception classes derive directly or indirectly from the System.Exception class, the base of the exception hierarchy.

questions.q: Programmer-defined (user-defined) exceptions should derive from which class?
questions.e: The System.ApplicationException class supports exceptions generated by application programs, so exceptions defined by programmers should derive from it.

questions.q: A catch block that specifies a parameter of type Exception will:
questions.e: Because Exception is the base class of the hierarchy, a catch block with a parameter of type Exception can catch all exceptions.

questions.q: The Message property of an Exception object stores:
o: the error message associated with the exception
questions.e: The Message property stores the error message associated with the Exception object; StackTrace, InnerException, Source, HelpLink and TargetSite provide other details.

questions.q: Which Exception property contains a string representing the method-call stack?
questions.e: The StackTrace property contains a string that represents the method-call stack at the point the exception occurred.

questions.q: If a program attempts to access an out-of-range array index, the CLR throws:
questions.e: Accessing an out-of-range array index causes the CLR to throw an IndexOutOfRangeException.

questions.q: Attempting to use a null reference causes which exception?
questions.e: Using a null reference throws a NullReferenceException.

questions.q: An attempt to divide an integer by zero raises which exception in the try block?
questions.e: Dividing by zero raises a DivideByZeroException, which can be caught in a corresponding catch block.

questions.q: When a new exception is thrown to replace an original one, the original exception object is stored in which property?
questions.e: The original exception object is stored in the InnerException property when a different error message or new exception type is used.

questions.q: SystemExceptions, which can occur at any point during program execution, are generated by:
questions.e: The CLR generates SystemExceptions (derived from Exception), such as IndexOutOfRangeException and NullReferenceException, which can occur anywhere during execution.

questions.q: When listing multiple catch blocks for different exception types, the general 'Exception' catch should be placed:
o: after the more specific exception catches
questions.e: Because a base-class Exception catch matches everything, specific exception catches (e.g. DivideByZeroException, FormatException) are listed first and the general Exception catch last.

questions.q: The Multiple Document Interface (MDI) was designed to:
o: simplify the exchange of information among documents kept under the same application
run multiple separate copies of an application
questions.e: MDI simplifies the exchange of information among documents all under the same roof: you can maintain multiple open windows within one application, not multiple copies of the app.

questions.q: In an MDI application, the main form that acts as a container for the document windows is called the:
questions.e: The main form (MDI Form) is not duplicated; it acts as a container for all the document windows and is called the parent window; the document windows are child windows.

questions.q: An MDI application can contain how many parent forms?
questions.e: There can be many child forms within the parent, but there can be only one parent Form.

questions.q: An MDI application must have at least how many forms?
o: two (a parent and one or more child forms)
questions.e: An MDI application must have at least two forms: the parent form and one or more child forms.

questions.q: Regarding controls, the MDI parent form:
o: must contain every control of the application
may not contain controls other than child forms, and usually has its own menu
questions.e: The parent Form may not contain any controls (other than child forms) and usually has its own menu.

questions.q: To make an ordinary (SDI) form into a child of the MDI parent, you set its:
questions.e: You make a form a child by setting the MDI Child property of that form to True, which associates it with the parent form.

questions.q: An MDI child form:
o: can only be opened within the parent form
must be a system modal dialog
can exist independently outside the parent form
questions.e: A child form cannot exist outside the parent form; it can only be opened within the parent form.

questions.q: When an MDI child form is loaded, its menu:
o: replaces the original menu on the MDI parent form
questions.e: When the child form is loaded, the child form's menu replaces the original menu on the MDI parent form.

questions.q: In the client/server model for web applications, the client's role is to:
questions.e: In the client/server model the client sends a request and the server answers the requests; clients may be thin or thick.

questions.q: In web applications, the server's role is to:
questions.e: The server answers the requests; for web applications the app is defined on a web server such as IIS, which may interact with a database server.

questions.q: Communication for web-based applications takes place through which protocol?
questions.e: Web-based application communication is through HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol); the client is typically a browser.

questions.q: A commonly named web server for hosting the application is:
questions.e: The application is defined on a web server such as IIS (Internet Information Services), which in turn may interact with a DBMS on a database server.

questions.q: The difference between static and dynamic web pages is that a dynamic page:
o: is generated (formed) each time it is called, according to the request
is stored only on the client
questions.e: Static pages do not change, whereas dynamic pages are formed dynamically according to the requests and are generated each time they are called.

questions.q: Saying that a web page is 'stateless' means that:
o: it does not remember the values of its variables between loadings
questions.e: A web page is stateless: variables do not 'remember' their previous values between each loading of the page, even though the page may be posted back to the server.

questions.q: Which of the following is a method to maintain a variable's state across page loads?
o: using a session/application state object, a static variable, a cookie, or a database
questions.e: State can be maintained using a session or application state object, a static variable (a C# feature), a cookie, or a database.

questions.q: In the URL http://sundown.wou.edu:81/en/mail.html, the ':81' portion represents the:
questions.e: In that URL, http is the protocol, sundown.wou.edu the domain name, 81 the port, and /en/mail.html the page/file.

questions.q: A browser displays pages that are defined using:
questions.e: The client browser displays pages defined using HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) tags.

questions.q: In an ASP file, server-side script is enclosed within which delimiters?
questions.e: ASP server-side code is placed between the <% and %> delimiters; within it, an apostrophe (') begins a comment line.

questions.q: In an ASP page, the statement response.write "Hello, ASP World!" causes the text to be:
o: printed to the server console only
written into the HTML output that the server sends to the browser
questions.e: response.write outputs its text into the page; the ASP code runs on the server and the words 'Hello, ASP World!' are written into the HTML delivered to the browser.

questions.q: After the server processes an ASP file, what the client actually receives is:
o: plain HTML with the script already executed and its output inserted
the raw ASP code including <% %> blocks
questions.e: The ASP code executes on the server; the client receives plain HTML where the <% %> script has been replaced by its output (e.g. 'Hello, ASP World!').

questions.q: The HttpRequest class represents an HTTP request and typically contains:
o: the HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.), headers, body, URL, and query parameters
questions.e: The HttpRequest class holds details of the request a client sends to a server: the HTTP method (GET, POST, ...), headers, body, URL and query parameters.

questions.q: The HttpResponse class encapsulates the response data, including:
o: the HTTP status code, headers, body and other metadata sent back to the client
questions.e: The HttpResponse class represents the response sent back to the client, encapsulating the status code, headers, body and other metadata.

questions.q: In ASP.NET, the HttpRequest class is part of which namespace?
questions.e: In ASP.NET, HttpRequest is part of the System.Web namespace and provides methods and properties to access request data.

questions.q: The key-value pairs from the query string of a URL are held in which collection, accessed via Request.QueryString?
questions.e: The QueryString collection contains key-value pairs from the URL's query string (often used for GET requests) and is accessed via Request.QueryString.

questions.q: The data sent in the body of a POST request (form fields) is accessed through which collection?
questions.e: The Form collection contains data sent in the body of a POST request (name/value form fields), accessed via Request.Form.

questions.q: The QueryString collection's key-value pairs are most associated with which HTTP method?
questions.e: QueryString key-value pairs come from the URL and are often used for GET requests.

questions.q: Response.Redirect() in ASP.NET is used to:
o: set a redirection URL and initiate an HTTP redirect to another URL
questions.e: Response.Redirect() sets the redirection URL and initiates an HTTP redirect, guiding users to another location.

questions.q: The HttpUtility class in ASP.NET provides methods primarily for:
o: encoding and decoding data (URLs, query strings, HTML) for safe HTTP transmission
questions.e: HttpUtility (in System.Web) provides methods for encoding and decoding data — URLs, query strings, HTML content — so data sent over HTTP is safe and correctly formatted.

questions.q: In RESTful API architecture, clients send requests to:
o: retrieve or modify resources, and servers send responses
questions.e: In REST architecture, clients send requests to retrieve or modify resources, and servers send responses to those requests.

questions.q: Which one of these is an HTTP Response collection (rather than a request collection)?
o: the Cookies collection (used to set cookies sent back to the client)
questions.e: Common HTTP Response collections include the Cookies collection (to set cookies returned to the client) and the Headers collection; QueryString, Form, ServerVariables and Files are request collections.

questions.q: The HTTP status codes 404 and 500 respectively indicate:
questions.e: HTTP status code 404 means 'not found' and 500 means 'server error'; such codes communicate error states to the client.

questions.q: Examples of HTTP methods conveyed in a request include:
questions.e: The HTTP request's method is one of GET, POST, and similar verbs, forming part of the request details in the HttpRequest class.

questions.q: Entity Framework is best described as:
o: an object-relational mapper (O/RM) that lets .NET developers work with a database using .NET objects
questions.e: Entity Framework is a tool to access a database — an object-relational mapper (O/RM) that enables .NET developers to work with a database using .NET objects.

questions.q: A major benefit of Entity Framework is that it:
o: eliminates the need for most of the data-access code developers normally write
removes the need for a database
questions.e: EF eliminates the need for most of the data-access code that developers usually have to write by hand.

questions.q: In Entity Framework, the context class derives from which base class?
questions.e: The context class derives from System.Data.Entity.DbContext (in EF 6 and EF Core); an instance represents a session with the database and Unit of Work/Repository patterns.

questions.q: A property of type DbSet<Student> in a context class represents:
o: an entity set (mapped to the Students table)
questions.e: A DbSet<T> (e.g. public DbSet<Student> Students) represents an entity set that maps to a database table.

questions.q: In Entity Framework, an entity is a class that maps to a:
questions.e: An entity is a class that maps to a database table; EF maps each property of an entity to a column in the table.

questions.q: In Entity Framework, each property of an entity maps to a:
questions.e: EF API maps each entity to a table and each property of the entity to a column in the database.

questions.q: In Entity Framework, 'CRUD' operations stand for:
questions.e: EF performs CRUD — Create, Read, Update and Delete — operations based on your model.

questions.q: Calling the SaveChanges() method on the context causes EF to:
o: build and execute the appropriate INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE commands based on entity changes
questions.e: EF executes INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE commands against the database based on the changes to your entities when SaveChanges() is called.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the Entity Framework entity states?
questions.e: EF entity states are Added, Modified, Deleted, Unchanged and Detached; the state determines which SQL command SaveChanges() issues.

questions.q: When SaveChanges() is called, EF executes an INSERT command for entities in which state?
questions.e: EF executes INSERT for entities in the Added state, UPDATE for Modified, and DELETE for Deleted.

questions.q: The Code-First development approach in Entity Framework is used when you:
o: already have an existing database and generate classes from it
do not have an existing database and create it from your entity/context classes via migration
design entities on a visual designer
questions.e: In Code-First you have no existing database: you write your entities (domain classes) and context class first, then create the database from them using migration commands.

questions.q: The Database-First development approach in Entity Framework:
o: generates the context and entities from an existing database
writes classes first then creates the database
questions.e: In the database-first approach you generate the context and entities for an existing database using the EDM wizard or EF commands; EF 6 supports it extensively.

questions.q: The Entity Data Model (EDM) consists of which three main parts?
o: conceptual model, storage model, and mapping
questions.e: The EDM is an in-memory representation of metadata made of the conceptual model, the storage model, and the mapping between them.

questions.q: In Entity Framework, 'POCO' stands for:
questions.e: EF creates an EDM based on POCO (Plain Old CLR Object) entities with get/set properties of various data types.

questions.q: By default, Entity Framework uses which concurrency strategy to protect against overwriting another user's changes?
questions.e: EF uses Optimistic Concurrency by default to protect from overwriting changes made by another user since the data was fetched.

questions.q: When reading data, EF translates LINQ-to-Entities queries into:
o: SQL queries for the underlying relational database
questions.e: EF API translates LINQ-to-Entities queries into SQL for the relational database (using the EDM) and converts the results back into entity objects.

questions.q: To insert a new record with Entity Framework, you add the domain object to the context and then:
questions.e: To insert data you add a domain object to a context (e.g. context.recipies.Add(abc)) and call SaveChanges(), which builds and executes the INSERT command.

questions.q: To delete a record fetched into 'abc' via FirstOrDefault, the commands used are:
questions.e: Deletion removes the entity from the set and persists: context.recipies.Remove(abc); context.SaveChanges();

questions.q: In the connected scenario of EF persistence, the same context instance is used to retrieve and save entities, which means it:
o: automatically keeps track of all entities and sets appropriate states, but keeps the connection open
questions.e: In the connected scenario the same context instance retrieves and saves entities, tracking them and setting states automatically (fast), but keeping the database connection open and using more resources.

questions.q: React is fundamentally:
o: a JavaScript library for creating user interfaces
questions.e: React is a JavaScript library (often compared to a framework because of its features) used for creating UIs (frontend), especially single-page applications.

questions.q: React is developed and managed by:
questions.e: React is open source and was developed and is managed by Facebook.

questions.q: React is used to create which kind of application?
questions.e: React helps in creating UIs (the frontend) and is used to build SPAs — single page applications.

questions.q: In React, 'JSX' stands for:
questions.e: React uses JSX, the JavaScript Syntax Extension, which lets you write markup-like syntax within JavaScript.

questions.q: React employs which kind of data binding?
questions.e: One-way data binding is one of React's listed features, along with JSX, components and the virtual DOM.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of React?
questions.e: React's features include JSX, components, one-way data binding, a Virtual DOM, embracing functional programming, simplicity, performance and being lightweight.

questions.q: Which command creates a new React application scaffold?
questions.e: A React app is scaffolded with create-react-app (e.g. 'npm install -g create-react-app' then 'create-react-app my-app').

questions.q: After moving into the app folder, which command starts the React development server?
questions.e: After 'cd my-app', running 'npm start' launches the React development server.

questions.q: React applications are built out of reusable pieces called:
questions.e: React uses components — such as header, footer and side components — as reusable building blocks of the UI.

questions.q: A web framework is best described as:
o: a software platform for developing web applications and websites
questions.e: A web framework is a software platform for developing web applications and websites, offering pre-written components, code snippets and application templates.

questions.q: In web development, front-end (client-side) frameworks deal with the part of the site that is:
o: visible to and interacted with by users
questions.e: The frontend is the part of the website visible to users (client-side), involving UI/UX design, SEO, reusable templates; the backend handles background functioning.

questions.q: The MVC architecture separates an application's concerns into which three parts?
questions.e: MVC organizes code into Model, View and Controller, separating user interaction, business logic and data — commonly used for UI-driven web apps.

questions.q: In the MVVM pattern, 'MVVM' stands for:
questions.e: MVVM stands for Model-View-ViewModel, an architectural pattern (an evolution of MVC) used primarily for building user interfaces.

questions.q: In MVVM, the ViewModel acts as:
o: a middle layer between the View and the Model, handling presentation logic and data binding
questions.e: The ViewModel is a middle layer between View and Model: it exposes data/commands to the View, handles presentation logic, and often uses data binding so the View updates automatically when data changes.

questions.q: The three-tier organization separates an application into which three logical layers?
o: Presentation tier, Business Logic tier, and Data tier
questions.e: Three-tier organization separates an application into the Presentation tier (UI), the Business Logic tier (core functionality/rules), and the Data tier (storage and retrieval).

questions.q: Push-based frameworks are also known as:
questions.e: Push-based frameworks are also called 'action-based'; MVC frameworks generally use this style, taking actions that push data to a view layer (e.g. Spring MVC, Rails, Django).

questions.q: Pull-based frameworks are also known as:
questions.e: Pull-based frameworks are also termed 'component-based'; they start with the view layer, which pulls outcomes from controllers as needed (e.g. JSF, Tapestry, Wicket).

questions.q: Which of the following is a back-end (server-side) framework?
o: Django (also Ruby on Rails, Express, Spring, ASP.NET Core)
questions.e: Backend frameworks include Django, Ruby on Rails, Express, Spring and ASP.NET Core; React, Vue, Bootstrap, Ember and Angular are frontend frameworks.

questions.q: Which of the following is a front-end (client-side) framework?
questions.e: Frontend frameworks include React, Vue, Bootstrap, Ember and Angular; the frontend languages are HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery.

questions.q: Which of the following is a push-based framework?
o: Spring MVC (also Ruby on Rails, Django, CodeIgniter)
questions.e: Push-based (action-based) framework examples include Spring MVC, Ruby on Rails, Sails.js, Django and CodeIgniter; JBoss, Tapestry, Wicket and JSF are pull-based examples.

questions.q: MVVM is described as being especially well suited for:
o: applications with complex UIs, particularly where data binding is available
questions.e: MVVM is more suited to applications with complex UIs, especially when data binding is available (e.g. WPF, Xamarin, Angular).

questions.q: In MVVM, the Model is responsible for the data and business logic and is:
o: completely independent and does not know about the View or ViewModel
aware of both the View and ViewModel
questions.e: The Model represents the data and business logic, retrieving/storing data and enforcing rules; it is completely independent and does not know about the View or ViewModel.
